I am 68 this year. I finished middle school back in the commune days, and I have worked this 7.5 mu of land for 20 years since my father handed it to me. My family has five mouths to feed, and every yuan I spend on fertilizer is real money out of my pocket. I have a well, so water is not my biggest worry, but a bad harvest means my grandson’s school fees are in trouble.

I split my land the same way I did last year. Four mu goes to wheat and maize in rotation — that is my stable grain income. The other 3.5 mu is vegetables: 1.5 mu eggplant, 1 mu chili, and 1 mu cabbage. Vegetables bring more cash than grain, but they rot if the price drops, so I never gamble the whole farm on them.

For my wheat on 4 mu, I plant the Jimai improved variety. Last year I got about 480 kg per mu, and this year I expect 500 kg if the weather holds. Before sowing last October, I ploughed deep and spread one 50 kg bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu — that is 7.5 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. At green-up in March, I broadcast 15 kg of urea per mu, which is about another 7 kg of nitrogen. If the wheat looks yellow at heading, I throw on another 5 kg urea. So my nitrogen ends up around 17 kg per mu. I irrigate three times: green-up, jointing, and grain filling. My well pump handles that fine. I spray pesticide twice, once for aphids and once for rust. I do not skip the ploughing before wheat — my father taught me that.

Maize goes on the same 4 mu right after wheat harvest in early June. I use Zhengdan hybrid seed from the dealer in town. I plant no-tillage because the summer heat dries the soil fast, and last year no-till gave me a good stand. At planting, I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the rows. At the big trumpet stage, I hoe in 20 kg urea per mu. That comes to about 18 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice — jointing and filling — and three times if July is dry. Two sprays for corn borer. I expect 550 kg per mu.

Eggplant gets 1.5 mu because my daughter-in-law can sell them at the county market. I buy hybrid seedlings in March at 0.5 yuan each, planting about 2,000 per mu. Before planting, I rotary till and put down 75 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. When the first fruit sets, I side-dress 15 kg urea, and another 10 kg urea when the second flush comes. That is about 22 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 12 kg potassium per mu. Eggplant drinks a lot of water, so I irrigate six times, basically every week in summer. I spray four times — aphids and wilt are always a problem. I expect 3,000 kg per mu.

Chili on 1 mu. I use an improved variety, not the most expensive hybrid, because chili prices jump around too much. I rotary till and spread 50 kg compound fertilizer per mu as base, then top-dress twice with 10 kg urea each time. That is 18 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu. Five irrigations. Three pesticide sprays for mites and thrips. I expect 1,200 kg per mu.

Cabbage on 1 mu. I plant autumn cabbage in July after pulling the early crops. I plough deep because cabbage roots need loose soil. I spread 60 kg compound fertilizer and 15 kg urea per mu at planting, then another 10 kg urea when the heads start forming. That is about 20 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu. Four irrigations. Three sprays for caterpillars. I expect 3,500 kg per mu.

Why these amounts? Because this is what I did last year, and last year was an okay year. The input dealer in town told me everyone in Quzhou uses 15-15-15 compound, so I stick with it. Old Wang across the lane uses about the same, and his wheat always looks greener than mine, so I am not cutting back. My grandson looked up something on his phone about balanced fertilizer, but I told him the dealer knows what sells, and the dealer sees more fields than any phone. Better to waste a little fertilizer than lose yield. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting half a bag of urea is just a cost.
